data.narrative:
QunaSys, a Series B quantum computing company founded by Tennin Yan, has raised $33M to date. The valuation framework considers a peer universe of 11 comparable companies across quantum computing: three public entities (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and eight private firms including Quantinuum, IonQ, D-Wave Quantum, Rigetti Computing, and Infleqtion.

Stage-progression methodology applies here, using the $33M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.9x multiplier typical for Series B advancement to the subsequent stage, yielding $63M. Peer-median analysis does not yield sufficient data; while six same-sector peers exist, none meet the confluence filters for stage-adjacency and valuation-tier comparability, leaving fewer than three datapoints in any narrow peer bucket. Applying an all-sector median would introduce material distortion given quantum computing's heterogeneous business models and maturity profiles.

The single applicable method supports a valuation range of $53M (low), $63M (median), and $72M (high). Key uncertainties center on the lack of direct same-stage comparables, which limits cross-validation of the stage-progression step-up multiplier. Additionally, quantum computing remains a capital-intensive, pre-revenue-dominant sector where traditional growth multiples and margin-based methods carry limited validity. This analysis should be supplemented by technology risk assessment and pathway-to-commercialization due diligence.
